German Metals & Mining Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Operations at Major Sites

DÜSSELDORF, Germany, June 14 — Thousands of workers in Germany’s metals and mining industry staged a walkout on Friday, halting production at numerous facilities, including the main plant of C D Walzholz International GmbH, as part of an ongoing dispute over wages and working conditions.

The strike, organized by the IG Metall union, began with early morning shifts and quickly spread to major mining and refining sites across North Rhine-Westphalia, Saxony, and Lower Saxony. By midday, union officials estimated that more than 5,000 workers had joined the industrial action, affecting at least a dozen mines and several processing plants.

“Workers are demanding a fair share of the industry’s strong recent profits,” said IG Metall regional leader Anke Schreiber in a statement. “We are prepared to keep up the pressure until our demands for improved pay and safer working conditions are met.”

Production lines at C D Walzholz International GmbH’s Hagen facility came to a standstill as workers walked off the job, leaving warehouses idle and ore stockpiles mounting. Company management confirmed that operations had been suspended and called for a swift resolution. “We urge both sides to return to the negotiating table,” said spokesperson Markus Feldmann. “Prolonged disruption could impact our commitments to customers and the long-term stability of our workforce.”

Other affected companies reported similar shutdowns, with several mining sites operating at minimal capacity and some smelters suspending their refining processes entirely. The industry association Bundesverband Metallbergbau und Rohstoffverarbeitung stated that the strike was causing “significant operational losses,” though it declined to estimate the financial impact at this stage.

Analysts said the walkout highlights mounting tensions in the sector, which has seen high demand for raw materials and metals drive up profits over the past year. “The workforce feels it has not benefited proportionally from the boom,” said industry analyst Jens Köhler.

Negotiations between IG Metall and employers are scheduled to resume next week. Union officials said the strike would continue until meaningful progress is made at the bargaining table.
